title: Isandro and the Cellar
premise: Isandro Amberdale, a pest controller whose real specialty is things that leave fingerprints where nothing walks, is called to Hollowfen House to keep the lights on and the doors counted. The house inherits its dead: each generation's keeper becomes part of the cellar's chorus, a song sung by the well that refills with everything the family refuses to mourn. When the mirrors begin reflecting the room one second late, Isandro realizes the delay is the house deciding whether he belongs in the picture. To survive, he must learn the song's last verse from his own late mother's handwriting in the cellar ledger without singing along, and choose between the duty he inherited from her and the love he finds with the house's last living heir, Maren Hollowfen. In the end he sings the verse silently, lets the well refill with his own grief instead of Maren's, and walks out at dawn with the mirrors running a full second early—time enough, at last, to leave.
about_author: W. M. Iversen is the pen name of a former building surveyor from coastal Norway who spent a decade cataloguing the structural failures of inherited houses. They write horror about the paperwork grief leaves behind.

chapters.title: Fingerprints in the Flour
chapters.summary: Isandro arrives at Hollowfen House on a routine call: dust disturbed in shapes no animal makes, prints pressed into pantry flour. He keeps the lights on and counts eleven doors where the deed says ten. POV Isandro. Beat: professional calm masking the first crack of dread.

chapters.title: The Client Who Won't Look Up
chapters.summary: Maren Hollowfen hires him for a month, refusing to meet his eyes and paying in old coins. She warns him never to answer the well if it calls his name. POV Maren. Beat: wary alliance forming between two people who both inherited something they didn't ask for.

chapters.title: Eleven Doors
chapters.summary: Isandro maps the house and finds the eleventh door only at night, behind the pantry, breathing cold. His chalk tallies vanish and redraw themselves. POV Isandro. Beat: the rules of the house reveal themselves as a job description he never signed.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: The hallway mirror shows Isandro's reflection lagging a beat behind him. He tests it with a dropped cup; the glass shatters a full second after the sound. POV Isandro. Beat: vertigo—the house is watching him with a delay, like something deciding.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Her Hand
chapters.summary: In the cellar, Isandro finds a maintenance ledger in his dead mother's handwriting, dated decades before he was born. Her last entry: 'Learn the verse. Do not sing.' POV Isandro. Beat: grief weaponized—the house has been expecting him his whole life.

chapters.title: Maren's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Maren confesses the family covenant: each Hollowfen keeper descends to the well at the end and joins the chorus below. She is the last, and the well is nearly full. POV Maren. Beat: tenderness kindling inside a death sentence; she wants Isandro to leave before it's his turn.

chapters.title: The Song from the Well
chapters.summary: At 3 a.m. the well begins the chorus—a round sung in many familiar voices, including one Isandro knows. He hums along without meaning to and his reflection stops lagging, as if pleased. POV Isandro. Beat: seduction; the song is beautiful and that is the trap.

chapters.title: Doors Counted Wrong
chapters.summary: The count changes: twelve doors, then nine. Maren finds a room that contains only her childhood bed and her mother, or the shape of waiting. POV Maren. Beat: the house rearranges itself around their secrets, tightening like a fist.

chapters.title: The Verse Nobody Wrote Down
chapters.summary: The ledger's last page is torn out. Isandro realizes the final verse exists only in the chorus below—learnable only by listening to the dead. POV Isandro. Beat: despair with a hinge of resolve; he begins memorizing without opening his mouth.

chapters.title: Neighbors Who Remember
chapters.summary: Isandro visits the village and finds the Hollowfens were never mourned, only avoided; the town once drowned a debt collector in the well and the family has paid ever since. POV Maren. Beat: justice outside the law—the house's horror has a human origin, and it was everyone's.

chapters.title: The Second Reflection
chapters.summary: The mirrors now show a second Isandro, standing where he stood one second ago, smiling when he doesn't. He covers every mirror; the covered glass hums the verse. POV Isandro. Beat: paranoia cresting—the delay is becoming a rival, or a rehearsal.

chapters.title: What the Well Refills With
chapters.summary: Maren shows him the well's rim: it fills with what the household refuses to mourn. Her ancestors fed it griefs, grudges, a drowned stranger. It is one inch from the brim. POV Maren. Beat: dread clarified into mechanism—when it refills, someone goes in.

chapters.title: A Night of Small Kindnesses
chapters.summary: A quiet chapter: they cook, mend a shutter, laugh once, and almost touch hands over the ledger. The house, for one night, counts its doors correctly. POV alternating. Beat: love against duty given its first real breath, making the coming cost legible.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Isandro finds the torn ledger page sewn into his mother's old work jacket, which he brought by accident. Her verse is half-legible; the final lines are written in a hand that isn't hers. POV Isandro. Beat: hope curdling—the verse was bait, passed down like an heirloom.

chapters.title: The House Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Through the mirrors, the house shows Isandro his mother below the waterline, singing, alive in the chorus. It offers a trade: Maren stays, his mother comes up. POV Isandro. Beat: the central temptation—duty to the dead against love for the living.

chapters.title: Maren's Decision
chapters.summary: Maren learns of the offer and prepares to go down willingly, believing a Hollowfen must end it. She leaves the coins, the deed, and a note in the ledger: 'Count the doors. Keep the lights on.' POV Maren. Beat: heartbreak as sacrifice; duty wearing love's face.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Isandro follows her into the cellar past the eleventh door, down stairs that were never in the survey, the chorus rising to greet them both. POV Isandro. Beat: terror and devotion braided; the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: At the well's edge, the chorus teaches the final verse note by note, and Isandro understands: it is a song of refusal, meant to be learned and never sung aloud. He mouths it silently as the well begins to refill. POV Isandro. Beat: climax of will—learning without joining.

chapters.title: The Refill
chapters.summary: The well takes its due. Isandro gives it his own grief for his mother, spoken not sung, and the water rises over the eleventh door and stops at the brim, satisfied. The chorus falls silent, one voice lighter. POV Isandro. Beat: climax resolved through surrender that is actually choice.

chapters.title: One Second Early
chapters.summary: Dawn. The mirrors now run ahead of the room. Maren is alive; the covenant is broken but not erased—the house simply has nothing left to collect. POV Maren. Beat: exhausted relief, grief finally allowed to be grief.

chapters.title: Closing the Ledger
chapters.summary: Isandro writes the final entry in his own hand: job complete, doors ten, lights off by choice. He and Maren bury the ledger at the well's rim and leave the coins for whoever comes next. POV Isandro. Beat: inheritance transformed—what he passes on is an ending, not a debt.

chapters.title: The House That Counts Itself
chapters.summary: Epilogue: a year later, travelers report Hollowfen House standing clean and empty, its mirrors a half-second early, its well brimming and quiet. Maren and Isandro pass through once, leave flowers, and do not go inside. POV Maren. Beat: peace with an open door—horror ended, memory kept.
